statusHistory.note: Operator-commissioned piece (chat request, named venue and address explicitly) -> trust: auto per rules.md trust-gate. near-write-article full pipeline run by PLINIO (historian byline, matches city-culture beat). Dedupe check (node scripts/check-duplicates.mjs) found no conflicting São Vicente entries. Research floor: near-deep-researcher-equivalent multi-source pass (8+ independent sources including the official IHGSV site, the city government's own tourism/news pages, Diário do Litoral -- an existing Tier-2 preferred source for the Baixada -- Revista Nove, Cidade e Cultura, ipatrimonio.org/Condephaat's state heritage listing, and a Dec-2025 IHGSV-produced YouTube video); Google reviews leg met directly (22 recent reviews read via Google Maps, browser tool, for garden/animal/practical detail -- no monkey mentions, confirmed volunteer-guide and on-site-cafe color); Reddit leg searched (site:reddit.com and general reddit queries) and returned no threads on this specific venue -- a niche municipal museum with no evident Reddit presence, logged as a null result rather than a blocked leg, substituted by the Google Maps UGC read. Operator's specific ask -- whether the garden currently has or used to have monkeys -- was checked explicitly against the institute's own materials, the Condephaat heritage listing (protects vegetation cover, describes it as a bird refuge, not primate habitat), regional press, and the 22 Google reviews: no source anywhere connects monkeys to this address. The one plausible explanation found: São Vicente has a separate municipal zoo-park, Parque Ecológico Voturuá, that turned up repeatedly in adjacent searches and may be what any such claim is conflating with this site. Verdict: UNCONFIRMED, not included in copy, stated explicitly in the body as checked-and-unconfirmed per the operator's instruction not to omit the check silently. III Festival Indigena de Sao Vicente (Aug 7-8 2026, this address) was verified current via the city's own July 2026 announcement, but was NOT nested as a dated child event page: the dates are already past relative to this piece's publish date (2026-09-16) and per the site's dates-out-of-evergreen-copy standing preference, no future edition date could be verified, so it's mentioned once in the body as a fact about what the venue hosts rather than pinned as an upcoming event. Images: near-illustrator equivalent resolved two real, high-resolution official photos (no generated/stock fallback needed) -- the city government's own tourism-page facade shot (2048x1365) as hero, and the city's own III Festival Indigena announcement-page photo (1600x1066, taken at this address) as the in-body image, meeting the ceil(500/250)=2 image floor for a 500-word body. Both are official-source photos with implied-consent licensing per this skill's standing photo-provenance practice, downloaded and hosted locally.
